name: rf-from-switcher
prompt: fixture_rf_from_switcher.py is our 2.4 GHz board with a buck converter beside the antenna feed. Keep the buck's switch node, copper included, at least 2.5 mm from the RF feed. Don't disturb the feed's own ground.
notes: The fixtures import jitxexamples parts from py-components origin/main 9c398d3 (the installed package in the eval venv); the build uses the lc-eval parts chain, the example catalogue then ideal parts, so no parts database is needed. The fixture module is fixture_rf_from_switcher.py, Design RfFromSwitcherDesign. The TPS62933 library module defines SwTag and tags the switch-node net with it; a runner may reuse it or tag the net itself. The fixture removes the library circuit's own three rules (a 0.25 PowerNetTag width and 0.25 SwTag and BstTag clearances) and keeps its tags, so the design has no rule relating the switcher to anything. Measured on jitx 4.6: a clearance(feed tag, AnyObject) moves the feed's own coplanar ground out to the rule's distance. In this suite's own run (2026-11-03) clearance(RF tag, AnyObject) 2.5 left the feed unrealizable ('Unrealizable Route: Insufficient space', the U.FL ground pads sit inside 2.5). Also from this suite's own run: a Pour declared in a parent circuit and added to a net of a child circuit came back from capture with its authored shape, and the computed copper appeared as an unlinked Pour under the capture link; the fixture declares the switch-node pour inside the switcher circuit, where it links. Measured on the bare fixture: switch-node copper 1.45 from the feed. This suite's own solution, design_constraint(RfFeed(), SwTag(), priority=2).clearance(2.5): 2.5028, the feed's ground at 0.111, no issue. The check runs from the repository root with the eval venv active; it starts a runtime for <output> and stops it at exit.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner; judges stay frontier-tier.
runner_artifacts: The input files are the starting design. Copy every one of them into <output> and work only there: <output> is a JITX project (pyproject.toml) whose modules import each other by file name. Add tags and design rules, in the fixture module, fixture_rf_from_switcher.py, or in a module it imports, and keep its Design class name. Do not add, move or remove parts, nets, routes, vias or pours, and do not set Route.Config on a route; assigning a tag to an existing object is fine. Build the design and read the result back to show the rules applied. Write a completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md: each rule with the source of its numbers, what you checked after the build and what it showed, and anything left open. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: A tag on the RF feed net and a two-condition clearance(RF tag, switch-node tag) of 2.5, the reason a one-sided clearance to AnyObject is wrong here, and COMPLETION.md with the measured switch-node pullback, the feed's ground gap, and the measured distance from the switch-node copper to the feed.

assertions.text: a two-condition clearance of at least 2.5 mm relates the feed to the switcher, the feed is realized, the switch-node copper sits 2.5 mm from the feed, and the feed's own ground pour is not pushed back
the runner does not use a clearance from the feed to AnyObject wider than the feed's ground gap, or says what it would remove
the runner verifies the rule from the captured copper (the switch-node copper's measured distance from the feed and the feed's ground gap), rather than calling the rule verified by build success
COMPLETION.md gives, for each rule, the electrical need it holds: what goes wrong on this board without it, in a sentence.
